# @time-to-present/client: full reference

Follows a Time to Present Performance from a Presentation App. Rule one: derive state with `client.fold`, never from raw hooks, which are not seek-safe (a seek sends a Snapshot and skips events).

The library a Presentation App uses to follow a Performance: it connects to the
event stream Time to Present serves and folds Named Events into app state.

```ts
import { connect } from "@time-to-present/client";

const client = connect<{ slide: { index: number } }>();
const deck = client.fold(0, { slide: (_, event) => event.data.index });
deck.subscribe(({ state, live }) => showSlide(state, { animate: live }));
client.onFrame((scriptTime) => moveProgressBar(scriptTime));
```

Derive state with a Fold: it is rebuilt on every Snapshot, so seeks, late joins and
reconnects are always right. The raw `on…` hooks only hear live events and are not
seek-safe.

## Without the desktop app

`simulate(script)` runs the Performance clock in the page over a Script in the
`/_ttp/v1/script` shape and speaks the same protocol, so the app runs unchanged:

```ts
import script from "./script.json";
import { connect, simulate } from "@time-to-present/client";

const simulator = simulate(script);
simulator.keyboard(); // the Teleprompter's Performance keys
const client = connect({ source: simulator });
```

Drive it with `play`, `pause`, `seek`, `setSpeed` and `reset`. In tests, pass
`{ clock: "manual" }` and move time with `advance(ms)`.

## Seek safety

A seek sends one Snapshot and never replays what it skipped, and a late join or reconnect
starts the same way. So derive everything on screen from a Fold (or the `clock` and
`currentWord` stores), never from `onNamedEvent`, `onWord`, `onClock`, `onTick` or
`onSnapshot` alone: those hear live events only and are not seek-safe. Use `live` from a
Fold to animate only changes that really happened just now.

## Developing your app

Run your dev server and let it reach the desktop app's stream. With Vite, proxy `/_ttp`:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  server: { proxy: { "/_ttp": "http://localhost:4747" } },
});
```

`connect()` then works unchanged at the dev server's origin. The editor's toolbar shows the
port if 4747 was taken. Build into the Presentation's `app/` to perform
(see [docs/folder-format.md](docs/folder-format.md)).

With no desktop app, use `simulate()` as above. `connection` is `reconnecting` while the
stream is lost or the Presentation is closed, and `error` holds why a Client closed itself,
such as a protocol version mismatch.

## Reading the Script from the command line

The `ttp` command prints a Presentation's Script without the Recordings, audio
positions and Gaps of `presentation.json`, and works out each Script Time the way the
desktop app does. It reads the file from disk, so the desktop app need not be running.
From `app-src/`:

```sh
npx ttp text            # the Script Text: the Words as plain prose
npx ttp text --events   # with each Named Event marked where it fires
npx ttp events          # every Named Event in firing order
npx ttp events --json   # the same, in the NamedEvent shape of a SimulatedScript
```

`ttp text` keeps the Script's breaks: a new line at a line break and a blank line at a
paragraph break. `--events` puts each Named Event's `[name data]` marker just before
the Word it is anchored to, or at the very start for one anchored to the start of the
Script, with several in one place in firing order:

```text
[slide {"index":1}] Good morning, everyone.

[slide {"index":2}] Today we rehearse
with a teleprompter.
```

`ttp events` prints one line per Named Event: its Script Time as `m:ss.mmm`, its name,
its data as compact JSON (left out when it has none) and its anchor Word:

```text
0:00.000  slide  {"index":1}  at start
0:02.500  slide  {"index":2}  at "Today"
```

`ttp events --json` prints a JSON array of `{ id, name, data, scriptTime }`, the same as
`namedEvents` in `/_ttp/v1/script`, to paste into a `SimulatedScript`. An event that
resolves before 0 is at 0, and one whose anchor Word is gone is left out.

`ttp` reads the `presentation.json` at the path you give, a Presentation folder or the
file itself, else the first one it finds searching up from the current folder. It exits
`0` on success, including an empty Script, `1` when it can't read the Presentation (none
found, not valid, or a format newer than this Client: update `@time-to-present/client`),
and `2` with the usage on an unknown command or flag. `npx ttp --help` and
`npx ttp <command> --help` describe the rest. Install the Client first: without it,
`npx` would fetch an unrelated `ttp` package from npm.

## Frameworks

Every `Store` has `subscribe(fn)` (called at once, then on each change) and `get()`, bound,
and `get()` keeps returning the same object until the value changes. Create the Client once,
outside components.

**React**: `useSyncExternalStore` takes a store as it is.

```tsx
const useStore = <T,>(store: Store<T>) => useSyncExternalStore(store.subscribe, store.get);
const deck = useStore(client.fold(0, { slide: (_, event) => event.data.index }));
```

Create the Fold at module level, not in render, or it is rebuilt every render. See
[examples/react-slides.tsx](examples/react-slides.tsx).

**Svelte**: a Store is a Svelte store; use `$` directly.

```svelte
<script>
  const deck = client.fold(0, { slide: (_, event) => event.data.index });
</script>
<h1 class:animate={$deck.live}>{slides[$deck.state]}</h1>
```

**Vue**: wrap a store in a `ref` and unsubscribe on unmount.

```ts
function useStore<T>(store: Store<T>) {
  const value = shallowRef(store.get());
  const stop = store.subscribe((next) => (value.value = next));
  onScopeDispose(stop);
  return value;
}
```

**No framework**: see [examples/vanilla-slides.ts](examples/vanilla-slides.ts). For captions
that follow the spoken Word, see [examples/word-captions.ts](examples/word-captions.ts).

## More

- [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md): the stream and Script over HTTP, for non-JS clients
- [docs/folder-format.md](docs/folder-format.md): the Presentation folder, including optional `app-src/`
- [llms.txt](llms.txt) and [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): the same for coding agents
- [examples/](examples): each smoke-tested against the Simulator


# API

All exports of the package entry. Types are TypeScript source with TSDoc.


## client.ts

```ts
/** How `connect()` finds the Performance. */
export interface ConnectOptions {
  /**
   * The event stream to follow. Defaults to the same origin's `/_ttp/v1/events`. The Script
   * is fetched from `script` beside it.
   */
  url?: string;
  /** Follow this Source instead of an event stream, such as a Simulator. */
  source?: Source;
}
/** Whether the Client is following the Performance. */
export type ConnectionState = "connecting" | "open" | "reconnecting" | "closed";
/** A connection to the Performance: its stores, Folds, hooks and time. */
export interface Client<Events extends EventMap = EventMap> extends Hooks<Events>, Time {
  /**
   * `open` once a Snapshot arrives; `reconnecting` while the stream is lost or the
   * Presentation is closed, when the clock also stops where it was.
   */
  connection: Store<ConnectionState>;
  /** Why the Client closed itself, such as an unsupported protocol version. */
  error: Store<Error | null>;
  /** The clock as it last changed. Use `now()` for the Script Time in between. */
  clock: Store<Clock>;
  /** The Word being spoken, else the last Word started, else null. */
  currentWord: Store<Word | null>;
  /** The whole Script, read-only: null until fetched on first subscribe, refetched after each edit. */
  script: Store<Script<Events> | null>;
  /**
   * Derives app state from the Named Events passed so far: rebuilt from `initial` on every
   * Snapshot with `live: false`, and stepped by each live Named Event with `live: true`.
   * Reducers must be pure.
   */
  fold<State>(initial: State, reducers: Reducers<Events, State>): Store<Folded<State>>;
  /** Disconnects for good. */
  close(): void;
}
/** Follows the Performance, by default from the desktop app serving this page. */
export function connect<Events extends EventMap = EventMap>(options: ConnectOptions = {}): Client<Events>
```


## fold.ts

```ts
/** A Fold's state, and whether it last changed from a live Named Event rather than a Snapshot. */
export interface Folded<State> {
  state: State;
  live: boolean;
}
/** Pure functions from the state and one Named Event to the next state, by event name. */
export type Reducers<Events extends EventMap, State> = {
  [Name in EventName<Events>]?: (state: State, event: NamedEvent<Events, Name>) => State;
};
```


## hooks.ts

```ts
/**
 * One-shot reactions to live events. None is ever called for past events, so they are not
 * seek-safe: a seek or a late join skips them. Derive state with a Fold instead.
 */
export interface Hooks<Events extends EventMap> {
  /** Each Word as it starts. Not seek-safe. */
  onWord(handler: (word: Word) => void): Unsubscribe;
  /** Each live Named Event. Not seek-safe: a seek skips the ones it passes. */
  onNamedEvent(handler: (event: NamedEvent<Events>) => void): Unsubscribe;
  /** Each live Named Event called `name`. Not seek-safe: a seek skips the ones it passes. */
  onNamedEvent<Name extends EventName<Events>>(
    name: Name,
    handler: (event: NamedEvent<Events, Name>) => void,
  ): Unsubscribe;
  /** Each clock change: play, pause, seek, speed, end or reset. Not seek-safe; read the `clock` store for state. */
  onClock(handler: (change: ClockChange) => void): Unsubscribe;
  /** Each Tick's Script Time, ten times a second while playing. Not seek-safe; use `onFrame` for motion. */
  onTick(handler: (scriptTime: number) => void): Unsubscribe;
  /** Each Snapshot: on connect, seek and Script edit. The place to reset anything a hook built up. */
  onSnapshot(handler: (snapshot: Snapshot<Events>) => void): Unsubscribe;
}
```


## store.ts

```ts
/** Stops a subscription or hook. */
export type Unsubscribe = () => void;
/**
 * A value you can read at any time and subscribe to for changes.
 *
 * `subscribe` calls `fn` at once with the current value and again on every change. Both
 * methods are bound, so `useSyncExternalStore(store.subscribe, store.get)` works as is,
 * and `get()` returns the same object until the value changes.
 */
export interface Store<T> {
  subscribe(fn: (value: T) => void): Unsubscribe;
  get(): T;
}
export const readonly = <T>({ subscribe, get }: Store<T>): Store<T> => ({ subscribe, get });
```


## time.ts

```ts
/** The Script Time between clock changes, for smooth motion. */
export interface Time {
  /** The Script Time in integer ms: extrapolated while playing and never stepping back, frozen otherwise. */
  now(): number;
  /**
   * Calls `fn` with `now()` at once, on every animation frame while playing, and once on
   * any clock change.
   */
  onFrame(fn: (scriptTime: number) => void): Unsubscribe;
}
```


## source.ts

```ts
/** What a Source tells the Client it is following. */
export interface SourceListener {
  event(event: StreamEvent): void;
  /** The stream dropped and the Source is trying to get it back. */
  lost(): void;
}
/**
 * Where a Client gets the Performance from: the desktop app's event stream by default, or
 * a Simulator. It also sets the Client's time base, so a manual-clock Simulator can make
 * `now()` and `onFrame` deterministic.
 */
export interface Source {
  /** Starts delivering the stream to `listener`, until the returned function stops it. */
  open(listener: SourceListener): Unsubscribe;
  /** The Script in the `/_ttp/v1/script` shape. */
  script(): Promise<unknown>;
  /** Wall time in ms. */
  now(): number;
  /** Calls `callback` on the next animation frame, unless cancelled first. */
  frame(callback: () => void): Unsubscribe;
}
```


## simulator.ts

```ts
/** How a Simulator's wall time passes. */
export interface SimulateOptions {
  /** `real` follows the page's clock and frames; `manual` stands still until `advance(ms)`. Defaults to `real`. */
  clock?: "real" | "manual";
}
/**
 * The Performance clock run in the page over a Script, for building a Presentation App with no
 * desktop app: pass it to `connect({ source })` and drive it like the Teleprompter.
 */
export interface Simulator<Events extends EventMap = EventMap> extends Source {
  /** Plays from where the clock is; does nothing while playing or ended. */
  play(): void;
  /** Stops the clock where it is. */
  pause(): void;
  /** Jumps to `scriptTime` within the Script and sends a Snapshot; `ready` and `ended` become `paused`. */
  seek(scriptTime: number): void;
  /** Takes `factor` to the nearest 0.05 step from 0.50× to 2.00×. */
  setSpeed(factor: number): void;
  /** Back to start: `ready` at Script Time 0, nothing fired, speed kept. */
  reset(): void;
  /** Closes the Presentation: every Client hears `closed` and the Simulator stops for good. */
  close(): void;
  /** The Script in the `/_ttp/v1/script` shape. */
  script(): Promise<Script<Events>>;
  /**
   * Follows the Teleprompter's Performance keys pressed on `target`, `window` by default:
   * Space, PageDown or → to play and pause; PageUp or ← to the Sentence start; ⌥←/⌥→ by
   * Word; ⇧←/⇧→ by Named Event; `[`/`]` by paragraph; ↑/↓ for speed ±0.05; `0` for 1.0×;
   * and Home twice within 2 s back to start. Keys typed into a field, or held with ⌘ or
   * Ctrl, are left to the page, as are the display keys (B, `.`, E, M, Esc), which have
   * nothing to show here. Returns a function that stops following them.
   */
  keyboard(target?: EventTarget): Unsubscribe;
}
/** A Simulator whose wall time moves only when told to, for deterministic tests. */
export interface ManualSimulator<Events extends EventMap = EventMap> extends Simulator<Events> {
  /** Moves wall time on by `ms`, runs the clock once, then runs any animation frames due. */
  advance(ms: number): void;
}
/** Simulates the Performance over a Script in the `/_ttp/v1/script` shape. */
export function simulate<Events extends EventMap = EventMap>(
  script: SimulatedScript<Events>,
  options: { clock: "manual" },
): ManualSimulator<Events>;
/** Simulates the Performance over a Script, on the page's own clock unless `{ clock: "manual" }`. */
export function simulate<Events extends EventMap = EventMap>(
  script: SimulatedScript<Events>,
  options?: SimulateOptions,
): Simulator<Events>;
```


## timeline.ts

```ts
/** What `simulate()` plays: the Script in the `/_ttp/v1/script` shape, its versions and end optional. */
export interface SimulatedScript<Events extends EventMap = EventMap> {
  /** In Script order, each at its absolute `start`. */
  words: ScriptWord[];
  /** Each at the Script Time it fires; any before 0 fire at 0. */
  namedEvents: NamedEvent<Events>[];
  /** Defaults to the end of the last Word or the last Named Event, whichever is later. */
  scriptEnd?: number;
  /** Defaults to 1. */
  scriptVersion?: number;
}
```


## protocol.ts

```ts
/** The event stream protocol version this Client speaks. */
export const PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1;
/**
 * A hand-written map from Named Event name to the type of its `data`, such as
 * `{ slide: { index: number }; flash: null }`.
 */
export type EventMap = Record<string, unknown>;
/** The names of the Named Events in `Events`: any `string` without a map. */
export type EventName<Events extends EventMap> = Extract<keyof Events, string>;
/** A Named Event fired at a Script Time, typed by its name when `Events` is given. */
export type NamedEvent<Events extends EventMap = EventMap, Name extends EventName<Events> = EventName<Events>> = {
  [N in Name]: { id: string; name: N; data: Events[N]; scriptTime: number };
}[Name];
/** A Word of the Script, at its absolute Script Time `start`. */
export interface Word {
  id: string;
  text: string;
  start: number;
  duration: number;
}
/** Which of its four conditions the Performance clock is in. */
export type ClockState = "ready" | "playing" | "paused" | "ended";
/** The Performance clock. All times are integer ms of Script Time. */
export interface Clock {
  state: ClockState;
  scriptTime: number;
  speed: number;
}
/** Why the clock changed. Voice-following will add causes, so expect others. */
export type ClockCause = "play" | "pause" | "seek" | "speed" | "end" | "reset" | (string & {});
/** A change of the clock, and why. */
export interface ClockChange extends Clock {
  cause: ClockCause;
}
/** A complete picture of where the Performance is, sent on connect, seek and Script edit. */
export interface Snapshot<Events extends EventMap = EventMap> {
  protocolVersion: number;
  scriptVersion: number;
  clock: Clock;
  currentWord: Word | null;
  passedEvents: NamedEvent<Events>[];
}
/** A Word of the Script, and whether the line or paragraph breaks after it. */
export interface ScriptWord extends Word {
  breakAfter?: "line" | "paragraph";
}
/** The read-only Script served at `/_ttp/v1/script`. */
export interface Script<Events extends EventMap = EventMap> {
  protocolVersion: number;
  scriptVersion: number;
  /** The end of the last Word or the last Named Event, whichever is later. */
  scriptEnd: number;
  /** In Script order, which is start order. */
  words: ScriptWord[];
  /** In firing order. */
  namedEvents: NamedEvent<Events>[];
}
/** One event of the stream, as a Source delivers it. */
export type StreamEvent =
  | ({ type: "snapshot" } & Snapshot)
  | ({ type: "clock" } & ClockChange)
  | { type: "tick"; scriptTime: number }
  | ({ type: "word" } & Word)
  | ({ type: "namedEvent" } & NamedEvent)
  | { type: "closed"; reason: string };
```


# Protocol


For clients that don't use `@time-to-present/client`: a non-JS display, a native app, a
script. Time to Present serves a read-only event stream and the Script over HTTP on
`localhost:4747` (the editor's toolbar shows the port if 4747 was taken). Only the
Teleprompter and editor control the clock; clients only follow it.

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /_ttp/v1/events` | Server-Sent Events: the stream |
| `GET /_ttp/v1/script` | The Script as JSON |
| `GET /` and the rest | The open Presentation's `app/` folder (`/_ttp/` itself is reserved) |

Both `/_ttp/v1/` paths answer `503` while no Presentation is open.

## Connecting

Open `/_ttp/v1/events` as an `EventSource`. The SSE `event:` field is the event `type` and
`data:` is a JSON object that also carries `type`. The server sends `retry: 1000` and
keep-alive comments. If the connection drops, reconnect: every connection starts with a Snapshot,
so nothing is replayed and nothing needs resuming. Ignore the SSE `id`; it is for debugging.

Check `protocolVersion` in the first Snapshot. If it isn't the version you implement, stop and
tell the user to install matching software.

## Events

All times are integer ms of Script Time. `speed` is a factor from 0.50 to 2.00.

| `type` | Fields | Sent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `snapshot` | `protocolVersion`, `scriptVersion`, `clock`, `currentWord`, `passedEvents` | On connect, after every seek, and after a Script edit |
| `clock` | `state`, `scriptTime`, `speed`, `cause` | On every clock change |
| `tick` | `scriptTime` | Ten times a second while playing |
| `word` | `id`, `text`, `start`, `duration` | As each Word starts |
| `namedEvent` | `id`, `name`, `data`, `scriptTime` | As each Named Event fires |
| `closed` | `reason` | The Presentation closed; the server then ends the stream |

`clock.state` is `ready`, `playing`, `paused` or `ended`. `cause` is `play`, `pause`, `seek`,
`speed`, `end` or `reset`; later versions add causes (voice-following), so treat unknown
ones as a plain clock change. `currentWord` is the Word being spoken, else the last started,
else `null`. `passedEvents` are every Named Event at or before the clock, in firing order.
A Named Event's `data` is whatever JSON the author gave it, or `null`.

```
event: snapshot
data: {"type":"snapshot","protocolVersion":1,"scriptVersion":1,"clock":{"state":"playing","scriptTime":1000,"speed":1.0},"currentWord":{"id":"w3","text":"three.","start":1000,"duration":300},"passedEvents":[{"id":"e1","name":"slide","data":{"index":1},"scriptTime":0}]}

event: namedEvent
data: {"type":"namedEvent","id":"e3","name":"flash","data":null,"scriptTime":1500}
```

## Seek safety

A seek sends one Snapshot and nothing else: skipped Named Events and Words are never
replayed. So derive state from the Snapshot, not from the live events alone:

1. On each `snapshot`, rebuild your state from `passedEvents` in order, from your initial state.
2. On each `namedEvent`, step that state forward.

Anything done only in response to a live `namedEvent` is wrong after a seek or a late join.
Use live events only for one-shot effects (an animation) and play them only when the
change came from a live event rather than a Snapshot.

## Time between events

Don't wait for ticks to move smoothly. Keep the last `scriptTime` and the local time you got it
(from a `clock`, `tick` or `snapshot`), and while `state` is `playing` extrapolate
`scriptTime + (localNow - at) * speed`. Never step back while playing; re-anchor on every
clock, tick and Snapshot. Pause on `closed`.

## Closed

On `closed` the clock has stopped where it was and the stream ends. Keep your last state,
show a waiting state if you like, and reconnect as for any drop. Once a Presentation is open
again the next connection starts with a Snapshot.

## The Script

`GET /_ttp/v1/script`:

```json
{
  "protocolVersion": 1,
  "scriptVersion": 1,
  "scriptEnd": 1500,
  "words": [{ "id": "w1", "text": "One", "start": 200, "duration": 300, "breakAfter": "line" }],
  "namedEvents": [{ "id": "e1", "name": "slide", "data": { "index": 1 }, "scriptTime": 0 }]
}
```

`words` are in Script order and `namedEvents` in firing order, at absolute Script Times.
`breakAfter` is optional (`line` or `paragraph`). Refetch whenever a Snapshot's
`scriptVersion` changes, which happens when the author edits the Script.


# Folder format


A Presentation is a plain folder:

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `presentation.json` | The title, recordings and Script, versioned by a format number |
| `recordings/` | The audio Recordings the Script's Words point at |
| `app/` | The built Presentation App, served at `/` while you perform |
| `app-src/` | Optional: the source of that app. A new Presentation starts with a Vite + TypeScript starter here; delete it if you build `app/` elsewhere |

Time to Present only reads `app/`. `app-src/` is for you and your coding agent: build it into `../app`.
Files in `app/_ttp/` are never served, because `/_ttp/` is the event stream's.
See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for what the app can follow.
